questions.prompt: Which set of functions is attributed to spontaneous communication in the researchers' conclusion?
questions.promptZh: 研究者结论将自发沟通与哪组作用联系起来？
options: Removing every disagreement and guaranteeing identical decisions.
Replacing the need for any shared context.
Creating more task conflict by preventing shared identity.
Supporting shared identity and context, and helping resolve conflict before escalation.
optionsZh: 消除每项分歧并保证决定完全一致。
取代所有共享情境需要。
阻止共同认同而制造更多任务冲突。
支持共同认同、共享情境并帮助在冲突升级前解决它。
analyses: A aids 与 contributes 不等于保证所有分歧消失或人人同决策。
B facilitates creation 是促进，不是替代。
C 方向与引文相反。
D 三个并列谓语分别提供认同、情境与冲突处理作用，仍保留单一公司团队调查及研究者解释的范围。

vocabulary.context: conflicts escalate 指冲突变严重，不是自动全部解决。
vocabulary.example: The team discussed the disagreement before it could escalate.

questions.evidenceQuote: Hinds partnered with Mark Mortensen to survey forty-nine teams in the research and development division of a single multinational corporation. The results showed that geographically distributed teams had far less spontaneous communication, less shared identity, and far more task conflict than those in geographically concentrated teams. Hinds and Mortensen concluded that “spontaneous communication contributes to a shared identity, facilitates the creation of shared context, and aids distributed teams in identifying and resolving conflicts before they escalate.”

questions.prompt: What topic does the sentence about spontaneity and adult friendship introduce?
questions.promptZh: 关于自发性和成年交友的句子引出什么主题？
options: Whether adult friendships always require exactly one formal appointment.
How opportunities for unplanned interaction relate to making new friends as adults.
A claim that all college friendships were randomly assigned.
A definition of every post-college friend as a close family member.
optionsZh: 成年友谊是否总要求恰好一次正式预约。
临时互动机会与成年结交新朋友的关系。
所有大学友谊都被随机分配的主张。
把每个毕业后朋友定义为亲密家属。
analyses: A 文中没有恰好一次预约规则。
B 后文对照大学反复非计划互动与毕业后来源，给挑战的主题。
C 不是友谊随机实验。
D 同事及孩子朋友家长都是可能来源，不等于全是近亲。

vocabulary.meaning: 带来另一项挑战；提出另一难题
vocabulary.context: 这里转向成年交友中的自发互动条件，不直接说自发行为本身必然有害。
vocabulary.example: The limited timetable poses another challenge for the group.

questions.evidenceQuote: Spontaneity poses another challenge when we try to make new friends in adulthood. What is the difference between college friends and post-college friends? College friends are the friends you lived in close proximity to, maybe even in the same dorm room, and with whom you had repeated and unplanned interactions. Your post-college friends might be coworkers or the parents of your children’s friends.

questions.prompt: What is the purpose of comparing college and post-college friends?
questions.promptZh: 比较大学朋友与毕业后朋友有什么目的？
options: To claim their closeness is guaranteed to be identical for everyone.
To count the exact number of friends each reader has.
To contrast friendship settings, including proximity and repeated unplanned contact.
To prove that coworkers can never become friends.
optionsZh: 宣称每个人两类友谊亲密度保证相同。
计算每位读者朋友确切数目。
对照友谊形成场景，包括距离近和反复临时接触。
证明同事绝不可能成为朋友。
analyses: A 问区别，不预设人人同样亲密。
B 没收集读者计数。
C 紧接 lived in close proximity 与 repeated and unplanned interactions 提供对照维度。
D 后一句还说 might be coworkers，不能否定所有同事友谊。

vocabulary.meaning: 近距离；住得或处得很近
vocabulary.context: 指空间接近，不能直接等同已建立的情感亲密程度。
vocabulary.example: Close proximity made informal visits easier.

Every post-college friend must be both a coworker and a parent of a child's friend.
The phrase refers only to the reader's own parents.
The sentence proves the reader already has children and coworkers.
optionsZh: 这些是毕业后朋友的可能来源，不是排他规则。
每位毕业后朋友必须同时是同事及孩子朋友的家长。
仅指读者自己的父母。
该句证明读者实际已有孩子与同事。

B 把 might 改成must、or改成and，双重过度限定。
C parents 的所属结构是 your children's friends，不是your own parents。
D 泛指阅读场景不是实际用户家庭资料。

vocabulary.context: 列为可能的朋友来源，不意味着所有同事都亲密或只有同事可交友。
vocabulary.example: Several coworkers joined the informal reading group.

Your post-college friends might be coworkers or the parents of your children’s friends.

questions.prompt: What does the question about becoming close invite the reader to consider?
questions.promptZh: 关于变得亲近的问句引导读者思考什么？
options: The exact annual salary of every new acquaintance.
Whether every adult has failed to make any friends.
How many names can be stored in a phone.
The depth of newer friendships compared with close college friendships.

是否每位成年人都完全交友失败。
手机能存多少名字。
新友谊相对于亲密大学友谊的深度。
analyses: A 不问收入。
B I would be surprised 是作者预期，不是对每个成人的失败证明。
C close 关注质量而非通讯录数量。
D 后句 as close as best friends from college 确立亲密度比较，不冒称已采集读者回答。

vocabulary.example: They hoped to become as close as their old classmates.

questions.evidenceQuote: How close have you become with them? I would be surprised if you were able to make new friends as close as your best friends from college.

questions.prompt: What is the role of the essay title in this passage?
questions.promptZh: 这段所列文章标题起什么作用？
options: It introduces a quotation attributed to reporter Alex Williams about friendship after thirty.
It names the49-team company survey.
It labels a clinical trial proving no friendship is possible after thirty.
It is the title of a novel about Moritz's train journey.
optionsZh: 引入记者 Alex Williams 关于三十岁后交友的引文。
命名49团队企业调查。
标记证明三十岁后无法交友的临床试验。
是 Moritz 火车旅行小说标题。
analyses: A In the essay...reporter Alex Williams concludes 将来源标题、作者与引文连起。
B 不是前一个团队研究。
C 记者评论不是临床试验，标题问难处也非绝不可能。
D Moritz 在下一小段是哲学假想例子，不是本标题人物。

vocabulary.context: 此处 reporter concludes 引出文章观点，不是说已实施新控制实验。
vocabulary.example: The essay concludes with a reflection on everyday friendship.

questions.evidenceQuote: In the essay “Why Is It Hard to Make Friends Over 30?” New York Times reporter Alex Williams concludes, “No matter how many friends you make, a sense of fatalism can creep in: the period for making B.F.F.’s, the way you did in your teens or early 20s, is pretty much over. It’s time to resign yourself to situational friends: K.O.F.’s (kind of friends)—for now.” At work, you might get close to someone from being on the same project.

questions.prompt: How is the sense of fatalism presented in Williams's quotation?
questions.promptZh: Williams 引文中的宿命感怎样被呈现？
options: As an unavoidable diagnosed state in every person over thirty.
As something that can gradually arise even when one makes many friends.
As proof that no reader can ever form another close bond.
As the researchers' numerical score for all company teams.
optionsZh: 作为每位三十岁以上者必有的诊断状态。
作为即使结识许多朋友也可能逐渐浮现的感受。
作为读者绝不能再有亲密关系的证明。
作为研究者给所有企业团队的数字分数。
analyses: A can creep in 保留可能，不是临床全员诊断。
B No matter how many...can creep in 描写数量多也未必消除这种感受。
C 引述评论不能升级成所有人未来不可能。
D 不属于前面公司调查的量化指标。

vocabulary.context: 比喻情绪逐渐出现，不是某个人实体潜入房间。
vocabulary.example: A sense of doubt can creep in during a long project.
collocations: a sense of fatalism can creep in

questions.evidenceQuote: In the essay “Why Is It Hard to Make Friends Over 30?” New York Times reporter Alex Williams concludes, “No matter how many friends you make, a sense of fatalism can creep in: the period for making B.F.F.’s, the way you did in your teens or early 20s, is pretty much over. It’s time to resign yourself to situational friends: K.O.F.’s (kind of friends)—for now.” At work, you might get close to someone from being on the same project.

questions.prompt: What is the scope of the statement about becoming close on a project?

options: Working together guarantees permanent friendship.
Only people in one specific television show can become close.
Shared project work is one possible way to become close.
Every coworker automatically becomes a best friend.

只有某个电视剧团队成员才能亲近。
共同项目是可能变亲近的一种途径。
每个同事自动变成最好的朋友。

B 当前句 At work 是一般工作例子，不只电视剧。
C might get close...same project 保留可能途径。
D 没有every或自动最亲密的升级。

vocabulary.context: 关系发展上的接近，不等于每次共事便有终生友谊。
vocabulary.example: They got close to each other while working on the exhibition.

questions.evidenceQuote: In the essay “Why Is It Hard to Make Friends Over 30?” New York Times reporter Alex Williams concludes, “No matter how many friends you make, a sense of fatalism can creep in: the period for making B.F.F.’s, the way you did in your teens or early 20s, is pretty much over. It’s time to resign yourself to situational friends: K.O.F.’s (kind of friends)—for now.” At work, you might get close to someone from being on the same project.

questions.prompt: What does the 'unless' condition say about staying in touch?
questions.promptZh: unless 条件对保持联系说了什么？
options: Being on another shared project is presented as a condition that can help continued contact.
Any shared project guarantees identical lifelong closeness.
Once a project ends, further contact becomes logically impossible.
The sentence says all workplace friendships are fake.
optionsZh: 再次共事同一项目被呈现为可助持续联系的条件。
任何共同项目保证终生同样亲密。
项目一结束，逻辑上就不可能再联系。
说所有工作友谊都是假的。
analyses: A unless...again 与 hard to stay in touch 表缺少再次共事时维持困难。
B 条件未保证感情恒定。
C hard 不等于 impossible，不能取消其他联系途径。
D 没否定既有亲密真实性，后面例子说明日常持续互动减少。

vocabulary.context: 可以有多种方式，当前句谈项目结束后的困难，不是绝对禁止联系。
vocabulary.example: We try to stay in touch after the project ends.
collocations: unless on the same project again

questions.evidenceQuote: But, unless you are on the same project with this person again, it’s hard to stay in touch. In the essay, Williams writes about a writer on the NBC series Up All Night who became really close with another woman on her team: “But as soon as the pilot was over, it was hard to be as close without that constant day-to-day interaction; there aren’t those long afternoons which bleed into evenings hanging out at the beach and then heading to a bar.”

questions.prompt: What additional complication is introduced by 'If you have a partner'?
questions.promptZh: If you have a partner 引入什么额外复杂性？
options: It proves every reader has a partner and children.
It says partners must already know all college friends.
It guarantees that partners reject every new friend.
The author adds a partner's liking of new friends as another consideration in his discussion.
optionsZh: 证明每位读者有伴侣和孩子。
说伴侣必须已认识全部大学朋友。
保证伴侣拒绝每位新朋友。
作者在讨论中把伴侣是否喜欢新朋友加入考量。
analyses: A If 是条件，并非真实用户家庭事实。
B 说new friends，不是全部旧友。
C must like 是文中所述协调需要，不推为必然拒绝。
D too 与 even harder 增加协调层面；这是作者论述，不是给每段关系制定普遍道德规则。

vocabulary.context: which 回指前述新增协调条件，不是断言每个人交友已绝无可能。
vocabulary.example: The meeting moved to another city, which makes it even harder to attend.

questions.evidenceQuote: If you have a partner, then your partner must like any new friends, too, which makes it even harder. When you add a child or two into the equation, making friends later in life can feel nearly impossible. In other words, after college it is really challenging to find someone who lives close by, with whom you can meet up every day and have spontaneous outings.

questions.prompt: What alternative is introduced by 'we could act spontaneously by ourselves'?
questions.promptZh: we could act spontaneously by ourselves 引入什么替代方式？
options: We must abandon all friends permanently.
Spontaneous action need not always depend on coordinating with another person.
Only group actions can ever be spontaneous.
The author reports that the reader has already travelled alone.
optionsZh: 必须永久放弃所有朋友。
自发行动未必总需协调另一个人。
只有集体行动才能自发。
作者报告读者已独自旅行。
analyses: A 提替代途径不等于排斥全部友谊。
B by ourselves 在多人约时间困难后提出独自可能。
C 与句中独自可能相反。
D 泛指可行性，不编造读者真实经历。

vocabulary.context: 此处着重不需他人同行，不是没有任何计划能力或不允许交朋友。
vocabulary.example: We can explore the question by ourselves before discussing it.

questions.evidenceQuote: Of course, we could act spontaneously by ourselves. The philosopher Jason D’Cruz has written about planned vs. unplanned actions using the term “volatile reason.” He considers a hypothetical person named Moritz as an example. In this scenario, Moritz has a ticket for a train ride from Berlin to Dresden to meet his friends.

questions.prompt: Who uses 'volatile reason' in a discussion of planned and unplanned action?
questions.promptZh: 谁用 volatile reason 讨论计划与非计划行动？
options: The reporter Alex Williams.
The team researcher Mark Mortensen.
The philosopher Jason D'Cruz.
The hypothetical traveller Moritz as the study's principal investigator.
optionsZh: 记者 Alex Williams。
团队研究者 Mark Mortensen。
哲学家 Jason D'Cruz。
作为研究负责人而非假想旅人的 Moritz。
analyses: A 来自前面交友文章的不同作者。
B 属团队调查研究，非此处哲学术语作者。
C The philosopher Jason D’Cruz...using the term 明确归属。
D Moritz 被说成 hypothetical person，是例子，不是研究负责人；当前片段未给术语的全部哲学定义，不凭外部想象补充。

vocabulary.meaning: 文中哲学家讨论计划与非计划行为时所用术语
vocabulary.context: 原段先介绍术语及假想情境，不将它擅自定义为化学挥发、经济波动或实测诊断。
vocabulary.example: The essay introduces the phrase volatile reason before giving its example.

questions.evidenceQuote: Of course, we could act spontaneously by ourselves. The philosopher Jason D’Cruz has written about planned vs. unplanned actions using the term “volatile reason.” He considers a hypothetical person named Moritz as an example. In this scenario, Moritz has a ticket for a train ride from Berlin to Dresden to meet his friends.

questions.prompt: What is Moritz's original travel plan in the hypothetical scenario?
questions.promptZh: 假想情境中 Moritz 原来的旅行计划是什么？
options: Berlin to Dresden to meet friends.

Berlin directly to Zittau with no prior commitments.
Zittau to Singapore for a concert.

B 起终点倒置且人物对象被替换。
C Zittau 是后面临时考虑的陌生城市，不能移到原计划。
D 混入别处城市；Moritz 是 hypothetical person，不是真实用户行程。

vocabulary.context: 限定为哲学家假想例子，不是观察到的真实实验或旅行记录。
vocabulary.example: In this scenario, the traveller has two possible routes.

The philosopher Jason D’Cruz has written about planned vs. unplanned actions using the term “volatile reason.” He considers a hypothetical person named Moritz as an example. In this scenario, Moritz has a ticket for a train ride from Berlin to Dresden to meet his friends.

questions.prompt: What makes the Dresden visit a plan with responsibilities?
questions.promptZh: 什么使 Dresden 之行不只是无约束的随意旅行？
options: Moritz has no friends expecting him and no tickets.
His friends are preparing dinner, and he holds concert tickets for their evening.
The train has no timetable or destination.
His friends have already cancelled every arrangement.
optionsZh: 无朋友等他，也无票。
朋友正备晚餐，他持有当晚与朋友的音乐会票。
列车没有时刻表或终点。
朋友已取消全部安排。
analyses: A 与 preparing dinner、tickets 相反。
B 两项预先约定由 in other words 概括为计划与责任。
C 时刻表是后句发现Zittau机会的依据。
D 取消是他后面想到可做的事，不是朋友已取消的事实。

vocabulary.meaning: 责任；对既有约定的义务
vocabulary.context: 在假设中来自朋友期待与票务安排，不是物理上不能更改任何决定。
vocabulary.example: An agreed plan can create responsibilities to other people.

questions.evidenceQuote: His friends are preparing a dinner, and Moritz has tickets to a concert for him and his friends that evening; in other words, he has a plan and responsibilities. On the train, however, he sees the train schedule and realizes that he could go on to the unknown city of Zittau if he stays on past Dresden. When the train arrives at Dresden, he spontaneously decides to stay on and visit Zittau, reasoning that he could just call his friends to cancel their plans and apologize.

questions.prompt: What new possibility does Moritz notice on the train?
questions.promptZh: Moritz 在车上注意到什么新可能？
options: He has already arrived at Zittau before reaching Dresden.
The original tickets were for Singapore rather than Dresden.
He could reach unfamiliar Zittau by remaining on the train beyond Dresden.
He must leave the train before Dresden to keep the original plan.
optionsZh: 未到 Dresden 已到 Zittau。
原车票去新加坡而非 Dresden。
若过 Dresden 仍留车上，可到陌生的 Zittau。
为原计划必须在 Dresden 前下车。
analyses: A if he stays past Dresden 说明顺序，不能把Zittau移到前面。
B 未改写原票目的地。
C could 与 if 保留一种可选后续路线，不是已经实现。
D 文中原定Dresden，不是必须提前下车；however 标出对原安排的新选择。

vocabulary.meaning: 越过 Dresden；经过该站后继续
vocabulary.context: past 在此为地点界限，不是说发生在过去。
vocabulary.example: They stayed on the bus past the usual stop.
collocations: go on to an unknown city

On the train, however, he sees the train schedule and realizes that he could go on to the unknown city of Zittau if he stays on past Dresden. questions.prompt: When and how does Moritz feel the reported freedom?
questions.promptZh: 所述自由感何时、怎样出现？
options: Before buying any ticket, as measured in a clinical trial.
Only after his friends have completed their dinner together.
As a feeling reported by every passenger on the train.
Immediately after leaving Dresden, he feels strong euphoria and freedom in the hypothetical story.

questions.evidenceQuote: Right after the train leaves Dresden, Moritz feels an overwhelming euphoria and a powerful sensation of freedom. D’Cruz argues that this was not a well-premeditated deliberate action, but nonetheless this spontaneous action served to fulfill Moritz’s deep desire to lead an interesting life. Spontaneity over responsibility. We can and should be like Moritz once in a while.

questions.prompt: What does 'Spontaneity over responsibility' summarise in this example?
questions.promptZh: Spontaneity over responsibility 在本例概括什么？
options: Responsibility and spontaneity are literally the same word.
Moritz gives priority to a spontaneous opportunity over his existing commitment in this scenario.
Every person must cancel every commitment on every occasion.
The example proves existing plans never affect other people.
optionsZh: 责任与自发性字面上完全同义。
该情境中 Moritz 把自发机会置于已有约定之上。
每个人每次都必须取消所有承诺。
例子证明既有计划从不影响他人。
analyses: A over 表优先取向，不是等同。
B 接假想转向Zittau及自由感，简短总结当次选择。
C 下句 once in a while 限偶尔，不支持every。
D 前文朋友准备晚饭已说明涉及他人；理解作者例子不等于无条件认可所有失约。

vocabulary.meaning: 优先于责任；在该取舍中压过责任
vocabulary.context: 是本例的概括性比较，不是时间或物理位置的上方。
vocabulary.example: In that fictional choice, novelty took priority over routine.

questions.evidenceQuote: Right after the train leaves Dresden, Moritz feels an overwhelming euphoria and a powerful sensation of freedom. D’Cruz argues that this was not a well-premeditated deliberate action, but nonetheless this spontaneous action served to fulfill Moritz’s deep desire to lead an interesting life. Spontaneity over responsibility. We can and should be like Moritz once in a while.

questions.prompt: What limits the recommendation to be like Moritz?
questions.promptZh: 像 Moritz 那样行动的建议有什么限定？
options: It applies to every promise a person makes.
It guarantees that no one else will be affected.
It is qualified as 'once in a while'.
It says no spontaneous action is possible alone.
optionsZh: 适用于每个承诺。
保证不影响任何他人。
限定为 once in a while，即偶尔。
说不可能独自随兴行动。
analyses: A 忽略频率限定，不能扩大到全部约定。
B 未保证行动无任何代价。
C once in a while 保留作者建议的偶尔范围。
D 前文正提出by ourselves，不应反转；这是作者从假想情境作的建议，不是实验结果。

vocabulary.context: 限制频率，不能删成总是或每次。
vocabulary.example: Once in a while, she chooses a different route home.
collocations: be like Moritz once in a while

questions.prompt: What does 'what we do for a living' refer to?
questions.promptZh: what we do for a living 指什么？
options: Work through which people earn their livelihood.
Only activities that are always entertaining.
The exact physical place in which everyone lives.
A rule that every person must have the same occupation.
optionsZh: 人们谋生所做的工作。
仅始终有趣的活动。
每人居住的确切物理地点。
每人必须同一职业的规则。
analyses: A do for a living 是职业谋生习语。
B 工作并非保证一直娱乐。
C living 在此非住址。
D Most of us 是一般倾向，不强迫人人同职业或都已就业。

vocabulary.context: 不是泛指活着的全部活动，也不是住在某地点。
vocabulary.example: She writes technical reports for a living.
collocations: what we do for a living

questions.evidenceQuote: Most of us strive to become better at what we do for a living. As a researcher, I try to stay up to date on the latest literature, statistics, data visualization, and so forth. This is all serious business. It requires careful attention, time commitment, and dedication.

questions.prompt: What does the author use his research work to illustrate?
questions.promptZh: 作者用自己的研究工作说明什么？
options: That all researchers use exactly the same methods and never change.
That reading literature removes all need to learn statistics.
That data visualisation is unrelated to his professional development.
An effort to keep professional knowledge and methods up to date.
optionsZh: 所有研究者方法完全一致、永不改变。
读文献便无需学统计。
数据可视化与他的职业提升无关。
努力跟进专业知识与方法。
analyses: A 自己try不等于所有人同流程。
B literature,statistics,data visualisation 并列，不是互相取代。
C 原句明确列入data visualisation。
D As a researcher,I try to stay up to date 给作者例子；latest 指所述持续学习，不是提供当前软件或研究清单。

vocabulary.meaning: 保持了解最新进展；不断更新知识
vocabulary.context: 本文指作者的职业学习努力，不是读者已经完成了任何软件更新。

questions.evidenceQuote: Most of us strive to become better at what we do for a living. As a researcher, I try to stay up to date on the latest literature, statistics, data visualization, and so forth. This is all serious business. It requires careful attention, time commitment, and dedication.

questions.prompt: What is called 'serious business' in this paragraph?
questions.promptZh: 本段 serious business 指什么？
options: Only commercial trading with a profit guarantee.
The professional effort and learning just described.
Moritz's exact train timetable only.
An assertion that all laughter is morally wrong.
optionsZh: 仅保证盈利的商业交易。
刚叙述的职业努力与学习。
仅 Moritz 的确切火车时刻表。
断言所有笑声在道德上错误。
analyses: A business 在此泛指认真对待的事，不是盈利保证。
B This 回指提升工作、跟进文献统计等，后句要求注意时间投入。
C 段落已转工作主题，不只火车。

vocabulary.meaning: 严肃而需要认真投入的事

questions.prompt: What possible cost of intense focus is identified?
questions.promptZh: 高度专注被指出有什么可能代价？
options: It guarantees all goals fail immediately.
It proves every professional never enjoys anything.
Much time can pass with little fun or laughter.
It means focus has no value for skill acquisition.
optionsZh: 保证所有目标立即失败。
证明每位专业人士从不享受任何事。
许多时间可能在缺少趣味笑声中过去。
意味着专注对技能获得没有价值。
analyses: A 没保证失败。
B easy for a lot of time...不是every professional永远如此。
C 当前句明确时间流逝与缺趣味笑声的风险。
D 代价可能存在不等于否定技能价值；接下来might one reason仍非单因确定诊断。

vocabulary.context: 当前指出的一种生活体验风险，不是测得所有人的永久状态。

questions.evidenceQuote: With this level of focus, it’s easy for a lot of time to pass without fun or laughter. That might be one of the reasons why so many of the world’s best athletes, such as Michael Phelps, Simone Biles, and Naomi Osaka, have suffered from burnout. They have talent, determination, and a ton of grit. Nevertheless, at some point the sports they loved became their jobs and livelihoods, sucking the fun out of the whole thing.

questions.prompt: What does the statement about talent, determination, and grit contribute?
questions.promptZh: 关于天赋、决心与坚毅的陈述补充什么？
options: It proves that all three qualities prevent every difficulty.
It denies that the athletes ever had abilities.
It says that a lack of effort is their only problem.
It recognises strong qualities even while discussing their loss of enjoyment and burnout.
optionsZh: 证明这三品质阻止所有困难。
否认运动员曾有能力。
说不努力是他们唯一问题。
在讨论乐趣流失与倦怠时仍承认其强大品质。
analyses: A 人物讨论正说明强项不保证无困难。
B have talent 是肯定，不是否认。
C determination与grit反对简单归因不努力。
D They 承接段中所举运动员，Nevertheless 后转向工作生计的体验；不据此为人物作新诊断。

vocabulary.meaning: 大量的；很强的（口语比喻）
vocabulary.context: 修饰grit程度，不是以吨称量人格或提供量表精确分数。
vocabulary.example: The project required a ton of patience.

questions.evidenceQuote: With this level of focus, it’s easy for a lot of time to pass without fun or laughter. That might be one of the reasons why so many of the world’s best athletes, such as Michael Phelps, Simone Biles, and Naomi Osaka, have suffered from burnout. questions.prompt: Why does the author acknowledge other important factors in the athletes' difficulties?
questions.promptZh: 作者为何承认运动员困难中还有其他重要因素？
options: To reduce every difficulty to dedication alone.
To claim all athletes share exactly the same biography.
To avoid presenting seriousness and dedication as the sole explanation.
To show that all previous achievements were invalid.
optionsZh: 把每种困难都归于投入一项。
声称所有运动员生平完全相同。
避免把严肃与投入当成唯一解释。
说明此前成就全无效。
analyses: A other factors与not just正限制单因归属。
B 原句in the case of分别对应不同人物经历，不能一概相同。
C 举其他因素并下一句not just，承认复杂背景；这是本书所述，不作新的个体临床判断或轻率单因归责。
D 经历困难不否定成就资格，亦不等于每个运动员有同一原因。

vocabulary.context: 引出书中给出的不同经历例子，不表示已列尽全部因素或所有人都一样。

questions.evidenceQuote: There are, of course, other important factors that caused their mental health issues, such as his parents’ divorce, in the case of Phelps, or sexual abuse, in the case of Biles. questions.prompt: What is meant by 'the bottom line' in the conclusion about elite athletes?

A rule that only athletes can ever experience pressure.

规定只有运动员才能感受压力。

B 习语非本句利润收入报表。
C 承认艰难不等于否定能力价值。
D 未排除其他职业压力；此处作者概括，不把所有人的具体病因或体验说成相同。
